description: The host's Claude and Codex subscription accounts (hostaccounts): list them; add one (Claude: name and an existing signed-in config folder, or name and token; Codex: name and an existing signed-in home, or name and token); rename one (id, name); replace a token account's token (id, token); remove one (id); disable a subscription or enable it again (disable: id, "" with provider for the CLI's own sign-in, and on: its chats' agents stopped, nothing sent to them nor started while it is); turn its auto-disable on or off (auto_disable: id or "" with provider, and on: disabled as one of its limits is used up or extra usage is billed, as its chats' turns or a usage read say, or at once if its last reading says so; enabled again only by hand); turn its auto-resume on or off (auto_resume: id or "" with provider, and on: a chat of its a usage limit stopped is sent a message to carry on a minute after the limit resets, unless it's disabled then); use another for a chat (session, id; "" for the CLI's own sign-in: its agent started again under it, resuming the chat, once its turn's over; kept as the one the host's new chats on its provider's models take, defaults); read a subscription's usage (id; "" for the CLI's own sign-in of provider, Claude's where none is said); sign in (sign_in: provider and name for a new account, or id to sign in to one again; Claude's runs claude auth login with the account's own folder, its lines coming as they're written, the page to open among them; Codex's codex login (method: the browser's, by default, or the device code's), its state coming as it goes (login: the page to open, and the device code's code to enter there); then its end; the connection's going stops it); pass a code the sign-in page showed to the sign-in this connection runs (code: no answer of its own); pass the address a browser ended on after a Codex browser sign-in's page to the one this connection runs (callback: url; answered with the page codex's server gave, or error). Each other is answered with accounts.

req.description: The request's number, the client's pick: its answers carry it back.

provider.description: add, sign_in (a new account): whose. usage, disable, auto_disable and auto_resume with id "": whose CLI's own sign-in (Claude's where left out).

id.description: rename, token, remove, disable, auto_disable, auto_resume, use, usage, sign_in: the account ("" for the CLI's own sign-in, disable, auto_disable, auto_resume, use and usage only).

session.description: use: the chat whose account it is, one of the host's sessions whose model is the account's provider's. sign_in (a Claude account's) and token: the chat it's for, whose sign-in (ChatLogin) its host moves as it goes, as a login request's, if the asker may read the chat (Agent Management's read).

name.description: add, rename, sign_in (a new account): its name.

token.description: add (Claude, Codex), token: what signs the account in, pasted: Claude's a long-lived token from claude setup-token (sk-ant-oat…) or an Anthropic API key (sk-ant-api…); Codex's an OpenAI API key (sk-…), written to a new CODEX_HOME's auth.json as codex login --with-api-key writes it. Kept on the host only, owner-only; never said back.

home.description: add (Codex): an existing CODEX_HOME on the host, signed in with ChatGPT and keeping its credentials in a file.

folder.description: add (Claude): an existing Claude config folder on the host, signed in (claude auth status says so, run with it).

on.description: disable: true to disable it, false to enable it again; auto_disable: whether it's disabled as it's exhausted. auto_resume: whether its chats a usage limit stopped are resumed as it resets.

code.description: code: what the sign-in page showed, pasted.

method.description: sign_in, Codex's: browser (the default: codex login, its page sending the browser back to the host's 127.0.0.1) or device (codex login --device-auth).

url.description: callback: the address the browser ended on (its path and query are what's passed on).

cb.description: callback: a number of the asker's pick, carried back on its answer (one sign-in can have several callbacks waiting).
